activities.prompt: How old was Alexander when he became king?
activities.reveal: He took the throne at 20, after his father was killed.

activities.title: Early life
pages: Alexander III of Macedon built one of the largest empires of the ancient world before he turned 33 [1]. Knowing how he did it explains why Greek language and culture spread from Egypt to India.
Alexander was born in Pella in 356 BCE, the son of King Philip II [1]. As a teenager he was taught by the philosopher Aristotle, who encouraged his interest in science and Homer's epics [2].

items.why: He was born in Pella, the capital of Macedon.

items.statement: Aristotle was one of Alexander's teachers.
items.why: Aristotle tutored him as a teenager.

activities.title: Taking the throne
pages: When Philip was assassinated in 336 BCE, Alexander, then 20, moved quickly to secure the throne [1].
He put down revolts in Greece before turning east toward Persia [1, 2].

items: Alexander puts down revolts in Greece
activities.explain: Birth in 356 BCE, schooling as a teenager, then the throne at 20 in 336 BCE.

activities.prompt: In two or three sentences: how did Alexander's early life prepare him to rule?
keyPoints: He was the son of King Philip II
Aristotle gave him a broad education
He acted fast to secure the throne at 20
activities.modelAnswer: As Philip II's son he grew up at the Macedonian court, and Aristotle gave him a broad education. When Philip was killed, he moved fast at 20 to secure power.

keyTerms.definition: An ancient kingdom north of the Greek city-states, ruled by Philip II and then Alexander.
Describes the period and culture after Alexander, when Greek influence spread across his former empire.
